name: Federal HPC
subtitle: DOE / NNSA / federal labs — tier-1 customer base

workload.primary_mix: Tightly-coupled MPI: climate and weather modeling, nuclear weapons stewardship, molecular dynamics, computational fluid dynamics, materials science. Growing AI-for-science workloads (surrogate models, inverse problems) layered on top of traditional HPC.
workload.typical_scale: 1,000 to 10,000 nodes per cluster at the lab tier; flagship systems (Frontier, Aurora, El Capitan) at 50K+ nodes.
workload.critical_characteristics: Collective-heavy communication patterns (AllReduce, AllGather, AlltoAll); strong-scaling sensitivity; long-running campaigns (days to weeks per job); multi-PI sharing with strict queue policies.
workload.latency_budget: Sub-microsecond MPI message latency required; tail-latency variance matters more than median — a single straggling rank stalls the entire collective.
workload.bottleneck_profile: Network injection rate and collective tail latency at scale, not raw bandwidth. Endpoint NIC behavior under congestion is the differentiator.
workload.buying_criteria: Predictable tail latency, mature MPI/libfabric stack, US-based supply chain (NDAA / Trade Agreements Act compliance), 10-year lifecycle support, established federal procurement vehicle (GSA, SEWP, ITES).

descriptions: CN6000 at 800 Gbps per port; one NIC per compute node
Native OPA protocol — purpose-built for tightly-coupled MPI collectives
Director-class fabric switch with up to 576 ports for fat-tree topologies
architecture.protocol_reasoning: OPA over RoCEv2 for tightly-coupled HPC: OPA has 10+ years of MPI collective optimization, predictable tail latency under congestion, and a mature libfabric provider. RoCEv2 requires DCQCN tuning per fabric and shows higher collective tail variance. UEC is the forward path (CN7000) but not production-ready for federal procurement cycles in 2026-2027.

channel.day1_isv_priority: Slurm topology-aware scheduling + libfabric OPA provider certification on CN6000 — these gate every federal procurement and are the prerequisite for HPE Cray EX-series integration.

tco.deployment_scenario: 1,000-node tier-1 federal HPC deployment — CN6000 SuperNICs + Director-Class switches
advantage_drivers: Lower per-port cost vs InfiniBand NDR/XDR director-class fabric
Mature OPA stack reduces ongoing tuning labor (illustrative: ~$300K/yr saved per analyst estimate)
US-based supply chain — no ITAR friction, predictable lead times for federal procurement

value_proposition.statement: Predictable tail latency at scale for tightly-coupled HPC, backed by a mature OPA software stack and a US-based supply chain that meets federal procurement requirements.

competitive_position.angle: Lower tail latency variance on MPI collectives; established federal procurement footprint; lower per-port fabric cost at director-class scale.
UEC ecosystem still maturing through 2026-2027; OPA has a decade of MPI collective optimization that UEC must replicate.
Generic Ethernet fabrics require per-deployment DCQCN tuning; OPA is purpose-built for tightly-coupled MPI workloads.

name: Academic HPC
subtitle: NSF-funded centers, university clusters — campus AI + traditional HPC mix

workload.primary_mix: Heterogeneous: traditional MPI (chemistry via GROMACS/NAMD/LAMMPS, climate via WRF, bioinformatics) on one side; AI training (campus model factories, research LLM fine-tuning, surrogate models for materials discovery) on the other. Single cluster typically serves both.
workload.typical_scale: 100 to 1,500 nodes per cluster (Stampede-3-class to mid-tier campus); multi-tenant fairshare scheduling; high job churn (10K+ jobs/day not uncommon).
workload.critical_characteristics: Heterogeneous workload mix on shared physical fabric; many short jobs alongside long campaigns; multi-PI accounting under fairshare; campus AI factories layered on existing HPC infrastructure.
workload.latency_budget: Sub-microsecond MPI for traditional HPC partitions; sub-millisecond AllReduce for AI training partitions. The fabric must serve both simultaneously without one starving the other.
workload.bottleneck_profile: Cross-partition resource contention more than absolute fabric performance. Small ops teams (1-3 admins typical) can't tune two physical fabrics — protocol flexibility on a single fabric matters more than raw performance.
workload.buying_criteria: Price-performance per NSF MRI / state funding dollar, fabric versatility across heterogeneous workloads, ecosystem breadth (Slurm + PyTorch both must work), operational simplicity for small staffs, ACCESS-allocation-compatible reference architectures.

products: OPA or RoCEv2 mode (configurable per partition)
descriptions: CN6000 at 800 Gbps, protocol-configurable per workload partition on a single physical fabric
OPA mode for traditional MPI partitions; RoCEv2 mode for AI training partitions
Cost-optimized switch tier (typically Arista or commodity Ethernet rather than director-class fabric)
architecture.protocol_reasoning: CN6000's tri-protocol mode is the genuine differentiator for academic HPC: a single physical fabric carries OPA for tightly-coupled MPI workloads (preserving the chemistry/climate stack performance academic users demand) and RoCEv2 for AI training partitions (matching the campus AI factory pattern). Academic CapEx budgets cannot fund two separate fabric tiers, and small ops teams cannot operate two — single-fabric multi-protocol is the segment's hard requirement, and it's where pure-InfiniBand and pure-Ethernet competitors both lose.

competitive_position.angle: Lower CapEx for the heterogeneous workload mix typical of academic centers; no need for a separate Ethernet tier when AI partitions grow.
Native OPA preserves the MPI collective performance that academic chemistry/climate/bioinformatics users explicitly demand and pure-Ethernet fabrics give up.
A single physical fabric is the only operationally viable choice for academic centers with 1-3 admins — dual-fabric designs lose to staffing reality before they lose on CapEx.

name: Enterprise Commercial AI
subtitle: Fortune 500 internal AI clusters — training, fine-tuning, inference serving

workload.primary_mix: Internal AI cluster mix: fine-tuning of base models (Llama, Mistral, Falcon) for vertical use cases; production inference for customer-service AI, document understanding, internal copilots; some pre-training for vertical-specific models. CIO-driven AI factory pattern.
workload.typical_scale: 200 to 2,000 GPUs per cluster; single-tenant (no rental); 3-5 year refresh cycles tied to enterprise IT budget planning.
workload.critical_characteristics: AllReduce-dominated training collectives (PyTorch FSDP / DDP); strict change-management windows; enterprise audit and compliance requirements; tightly-controlled vendor relationships through OEM bundling.
workload.latency_budget: Sub-millisecond AllReduce gates training throughput at scale; tail latency matters for online inference SLAs.
workload.bottleneck_profile: Fabric bandwidth and collective efficiency for training; tail latency for inference. NVIDIA Spectrum-X bundled fabric is the strategic competitor — enterprise customers value bundled solutions more than absolute performance.
workload.buying_criteria: Enterprise OEM support model (Dell, Lenovo, HPE relationships own the buying motion), Ethernet ecosystem familiarity (existing data-center skillset), NVIDIA GPU compatibility, audit/compliance posture for production AI, vendor-diversification asks from CIOs concerned about NVIDIA lock-in.

descriptions: CN6000 at 800 Gbps in RoCEv2 mode — drops into existing enterprise Ethernet fabrics with no separate fabric tier
Compatible with standard data-center switching from enterprise-vetted vendors (Arista, Cisco, Juniper)
Endpoint NIC congestion behavior optimized for AI AllReduce patterns (DCQCN-standard plus Cornelis-specific tail-variance handling)
architecture.protocol_reasoning: Enterprise AI is the RoCEv2-native segment by definition — the customer's existing fabric is Ethernet, the ops team's skillset is Ethernet, and the vendor support model is Ethernet-centric. Switching to InfiniBand requires a parallel fabric tier (incremental CapEx) plus an InfiniBand-trained ops team (incremental headcount) — most enterprise CIOs reject both. Cornelis's RoCEv2 advantage is endpoint NIC behavior under congestion: standard merchant-silicon NICs require per-fabric DCQCN tuning that becomes operationally painful at scale, while CN6000 endpoint behavior reduces tail-latency variance without per-fabric ops investment. UEC is the forward-looking story, but enterprise procurement cycles run 3-5 years — CN6000 RoCEv2 is the workhorse through ~2028.

name: Neoclouds
subtitle: GPU-as-a-service operators — CoreWeave, Lambda, Together, Crusoe, RunPod class

workload.primary_mix: Multi-tenant GPU rental for AI training (the dominant load), with growing inference-as-a-service at the platform edge. Customer mix includes AI labs (Anthropic-class), AI-native enterprises, and increasingly NVIDIA-competitive accelerator customers (AMD MI300, AWS Trainium adopters). PyTorch FSDP / DDP is the dominant collective pattern.
workload.typical_scale: 1,000 to 50,000 GPUs per region; aggressive multi-region build cadence (new pod every 3-6 months for tier-1 operators); single-tenant from the customer perspective but multi-customer from the operator perspective.
workload.critical_characteristics: Time-to-revenue on new build-outs (every week of build delay is direct revenue impact); multi-tenancy isolation between customers; per-GPU economics dominate operator margin; high build cadence requires repeatable reference architecture.
workload.latency_budget: Sub-millisecond AllReduce for training collectives — gates customer-visible training throughput; bandwidth maximization at rack level for FSDP shard exchange.
workload.bottleneck_profile: Per-GPU fabric CapEx and operational simplicity dominate. NVIDIA NDR / XDR fabric premium directly compresses operator margin. Build cadence (how fast can you stand up the next 10K-GPU pod, including fabric tuning) is the operational constraint.
workload.buying_criteria: $/GPU fabric cost, supply lead time, protocol flexibility for UEC migration path, open-standards alignment (operators reject NVIDIA lock-in for strategic margin and customer-mix reasons), repeatable reference architecture for fast build cadence.

descriptions: CN6000 at 800 Gbps in RoCEv2 mode — drops into standard high-density Ethernet fabrics with no NVIDIA-only switching tier
UEC roadmap commit (CN7000 at 1.6T) aligns with neocloud operator preference for open standards
Dense rack designs (8-16 GPU per node, multiple NICs per node) optimized for $/GPU economics at hyperscale-class neocloud builds
architecture.protocol_reasoning: Neoclouds reject NVIDIA stack lock-in for two structural reasons: (1) operator margin compression argues against NVIDIA-bundled Spectrum-X pricing; (2) the customer mix increasingly includes NVIDIA-competitive accelerator buyers (AMD MI300, Trainium) who want operator infrastructure that doesn't presuppose CUDA + InfiniBand. CN6000 RoCEv2 mode meets the today requirement; the CN7000 UEC commit meets the strategic preference for the open-standards path. UEC matters specifically because it removes NVIDIA control over the next-gen collective standard — Cornelis chairs UEC working groups, and CN7000 will be among the first production 1.6T UEC chips in 2027-2028. Neoclouds buy the roadmap, not just the current part.

name: Sovereign AI
subtitle: Nation-state and regional AI infrastructure — compliance, supply-chain provenance, vendor independence

workload.primary_mix: National-language LLM training and fine-tuning (Mistral / EU sovereign models, regional language models in APAC and Middle East), government-services AI deployment, compliance-sensitive enterprise workloads tied to national programs. Distinct from federal HPC (which is science compute) and enterprise AI (which is commercial).
workload.typical_scale: 200 to 2,000 nodes per deployment; multi-year commitments tied to national program timelines (3-5 year horizons typical); often phased pilot → expansion → full-scale.
workload.critical_characteristics: Data residency requirements (workload and storage stay within national borders), supply chain provenance (NDAA / Trade Agreements Act / EU procurement compliance), vendor independence from US-China tension axis, regulated procurement timelines (12-24 months typical).
workload.latency_budget: AI training collectives — not latency-pathological but throughput-sensitive; regional-language fine-tuning workloads tolerate slightly higher AllReduce latency than tier-1 frontier-model training.
workload.bottleneck_profile: Procurement timeline (regulatory approvals) and supply chain provenance dominate over raw fabric performance. The bottleneck is rarely the network — it's getting the contract through compliance review.
workload.buying_criteria: Supply chain provenance (US-based or allied-nation, NDAA-clean), long-term roadmap visibility (3-5 year procurement requires confidence in the vendor's product roadmap), protocol independence (avoid NVIDIA lock-in for strategic reasons), regional integrator partnership (deployment depends on local SI relationships).

products: Regional integrator-selected fabric tier (region-dependent: Arista in EU, NTT/Hitachi-supported tiers in APAC)
descriptions: CN6000 at 800 Gbps in RoCEv2 mode — aligns with sovereign AI workload profile (AI training-dominant, not tightly-coupled MPI)
Federally-cleared US-based supply chain meets NDAA / Trade Agreements Act / allied-nation sovereign procurement requirements
Pairs with regional integrator switch and server tier — sovereign deployments require named local partners as a procurement prerequisite
architecture.protocol_reasoning: Same RoCEv2 protocol fit as Enterprise AI — sovereign AI training workloads are Ethernet-native, not OPA-native. But the value proposition is structurally different: sovereign customers explicitly value (1) US-based supply chain provenance (NDAA-clean meets allied-nation procurement standards in a way Chinese-origin alternatives cannot), (2) vendor independence from NVIDIA stack (many EU sovereign programs explicitly require non-NVIDIA NIC options), and (3) open-standards alignment via UEC commit (strategic hedge against US export controls for allied-nation buyers). Protocol independence here means buyer audit-ability, not performance — sovereign programs need to inspect and certify the fabric stack, which proprietary US-vendor InfiniBand makes harder.
